from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Hash functions are digital fingerprints for data.", "They are simple to compute one way.", "They are impossible to reverse."]
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: Cryptographic Hash Functions", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        hash_box = Rectangle(width=2, height=1, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(hash_box, 'C3')
        hash_label = Text("Hash Box", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        hash_label.next_to(hash_box, UP)
        
        input_data = Text("Blockchain", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(input_data, 'B2')
        
        output_data = Text("a1b2", font_size=24, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(output_data, 'D4')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(hash_box), Write(hash_label))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(input_data), input_data.animate.move_to(hash_box.get_center()))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(output_data))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Proof-of-Work Math: Solving the Puzzle", [
            "Bitcoin requires solving SHA-256 puzzles.", 
            "Miners find a nonce for valid hashes.", 
            "Difficulty ensures a ten-minute block time."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FF00")
        nonce_label = Text("Nonce:", font_size=36, color=WHITE)
        nonce_val = Integer(0, font_size=36, color="#00FF00")
        nonce_group = VGroup(nonce_label, nonce_val).arrange(RIGHT)
        self.place_at_grid(nonce_group, 'B2')
        self.add(nonce_group)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        hash_label = Text("Hash:", font_size=36, color=WHITE)
        hash_val = Text("0000a1b2...", font_size=36, color=WHITE)
        hash_group = VGroup(hash_label, hash_val).arrange(RIGHT)
        self.place_at_grid(hash_group, 'C2')
        self.add(hash_group)
        
        # Simulate incrementing nonce and hash change
        for i in range(10):
            nonce_val.set_value(i * 12345)
            self.wait(0.1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        hash_val.set_text("0000c3d4...")
        hash_val.set_color("#FF0000")
        
        diff_label = Text("Difficulty: 10 mins", font_size=36, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(diff_label, 'D2')
        self.add(diff_label)
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Private keys are secret numbers.", "Public keys are derived elliptic points.", "They enable secure digital ownership."]
        self.setup_layout("Public-Key Cryptography: Who Owns the Coins?", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        private_key = Circle(radius=0.3, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.5)
        pk_label = Text("Private Key", font_size=18).next_to(private_key, DOWN)
        priv_group = VGroup(private_key, pk_label)
        
        public_key = Dot(color=BLUE, radius=0.15)
        pub_label = Text("Public Key", font_size=18).next_to(public_key, DOWN)
        pub_group = VGroup(public_key, pub_label)
        
        vault = Rectangle(height=1.5, width=2, color=WHITE)
        vault_label = Text("Digital Wallet", font_size=18).next_to(vault, UP)
        wallet = VGroup(vault, vault_label)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(priv_group))
        self.place_at_grid(priv_group, 'B2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(pub_group))
        self.place_at_grid(pub_group, 'B5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.place_at_grid(wallet, 'E4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(wallet))
        self.play(
            priv_group.animate.move_to(self.grid['E3']),
            pub_group.animate.move_to(self.grid['E5'])
        )
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Digital Signatures: Proving Ownership", [
            "Private keys seal digital transactions.",
            "Public keys verify the signatures.",
            "Originality remains protected throughout."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        data = Rectangle(width=2, height=1.5, color=WHITE)
        data_label = Text("Transaction Data", font_size=20).next_to(data, UP)
        data_group = VGroup(data, data_label)
        
        priv_key = Circle(radius=0.5, color=YELLOW)
        priv_label = Text("Private Key", font_size=18).next_to(priv_key, DOWN)
        priv_group = VGroup(priv_key, priv_label)
        
        signature = Star(color="#FF00FF", inner_radius=0.2, outer_radius=0.5)
        sig_label = Text("Signature", font_size=18).next_to(signature, DOWN)
        sig_group = VGroup(signature, sig_label)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(data_group))
        self.place_in_area(data_group, "B2", "C3")
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(priv_group))
        self.place_at_grid(priv_group, "E2")
        self.play(priv_group.animate.move_to(data.get_center()))
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(priv_group, sig_group))
        self.place_in_area(sig_group, "B4", "C5")
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(Flash(sig_group, color="#FF00FF"))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion: The Security of the Chain", [
            "Hashing binds transactions into chains.",
            "Changing data breaks the hash link.",
            "The chain remains immutable and secure."
        ])
        
        # Helper to create a block
        def create_block(color):
            return Rectangle(width=1, height=0.6, color=color, fill_opacity=0.6)

        blocks = VGroup(
            create_block(BLUE),
            create_block(GREEN),
            create_block(YELLOW)
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(FadeIn(blocks))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(RED))
        
        # Simulate tampering
        tamper_flash = Flash(blocks[1].get_center(), color=RED)
        self.play(tamper_flash)
        self.play(blocks[1].animate.set_color(RED))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        immutable_text = Text("IMMUTABLE", font_size=40, color=WHITE).set_stroke(width=2)
        self.place_at_grid(immutable_text, 'E3')
        self.play(Write(immutable_text))
        self.wait(2)

outline.target_audience: University students with a basic interest in computer science and cryptography

sections.title: Introduction: Cryptographic Hash Functions
sections.content: Define hashing as a digital fingerprint. Explain the concept of a 'one-way function'—easy to compute in one direction, impossible to reverse.
sections.example: Imagine a 'Magic Blender': You can put a whole fruit salad in and get a unique 64-character smoothie recipe, but you can never turn the smoothie back into the original fruit.

sections.title: The Proof-of-Work Math: Solving the Puzzle
sections.content: Introduce the SHA-256 algorithm. Explain that Bitcoin requires finding a specific 'nonce' (a random number) that, when combined with transaction data, produces a hash starting with a specific number of zeros.
sections.example: A digital treasure hunt: Miners are like monkeys at typewriters trying to find the one password that opens a digital lock, where the difficulty is adjusted to ensure it takes 10 minutes.

sections.title: Public-Key Cryptography: Who Owns the Coins?
sections.content: Explain Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC). Introduce the relationship between a Private Key (a secret number) and a Public Key (a point on an elliptic curve derived from the private key).
sections.example: Use a 'Lock and Key' analogy: Your Private Key is the secret key to open the vault, and your Public Key is the transparent glass address box where people can safely deposit gold bars.

sections.title: Digital Signatures: Proving Ownership
sections.content: Demonstrate how the Private Key acts as a mathematical 'seal' on a transaction. The network uses the Public Key to verify the signature without ever seeing the Private Key.
sections.example: A magical wax seal: You use your ring (Private Key) to stamp a document; anyone in the village can use your public portrait (Public Key) to verify the seal belongs to you, without knowing how you crafted the ring.

sections.title: Conclusion: The Security of the Chain
sections.content: Summarize how hashing and ECC bind transactions into an immutable chain. If one piece of data changes, the hash changes, breaking the chain.
sections.example: The 'Lego Tower': Every block is a brick. If you try to swap a brick in the middle, the entire tower above it becomes unstable and alerts everyone that the structure has been tampered with.
